messages:
sara: Quick Q — ran canary for the param-change branch and hit a weird case: when a stop sequence fires mid-token during streaming the response sometimes comes back with logprobs=null. Also seeing cases where max_tokens truncation + stop interact and the termination token isn't included in the final text. Anyone seen this? cc @liam

ben: Hmm that's concerning. Which model and runner?

sara: llama-70b-q8 on dedicated-canary. Repro: prompt ends with '### END', stop=["### END"], max_tokens=20, temperature=0.2, top_p=0.95, streaming=true, logprobs=5. Sometimes we get a partial token and logprobs==null.

liam: Sounds like a streaming truncation race — we probably flush the event before recomputing logprobs. Could be a postprocess ordering bug.

ben: Can you paste a minimal repro and the PR/branch?

sara: Minimal repro: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"llama-70b-q8","input":"...### END","stop":["### END"],"max_tokens":20,"temperature":0.2,"top_p":0.95,"stream":true,"logprobs":5}'```
PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/2109

ci-bot: CI (canary) for branch param-fix: 42/43 tests passed. Failing: tests/test_stream_logprob.py::test_stop_mid_token (flaky failure reproducing reported issue).

sara: Test snippet: ```python
def test_stop_mid_token():
  resp = client.generate(..., stream=True, logprobs=5)
  assert resp.choices[0].logprobs is not None
```
Fail shows resp.choices[0].logprobs == None when stop caused truncation mid-token.

liam: I'll take this. My guess: streaming path emits final chunk after truncation but before logprob aggregation. Two options: recompute last-token logprobs after truncation, or ensure we compute logprobs before emitting the final truncated chunk.

ben: Also think about backward compatibility — some clients implicitly treated missing logprobs as a signal. If we change behavior we should document.

anna: From product POV — is this a breaking change? Some customers use absence of logprobs to detect truncation. We need a migration note and maybe an opt-in.

ben: Proposal: add a flag `compute_logprobs_on_termination` (true|false) defaulting to true for the new canary. Ship code that recomputes by default, add docs and deprecation note. For Dedicated customers we can expose a config toggle.

sara: Sounds good. I updated the PR with an integration test that asserts logprobs exist for both stop and max_tokens termination.

liam: I'll open a tiny patch to recompute logprobs at stream termination and emit a perf metric. If recompute causes >2% change to p50 token latency on the runner we'll gate it behind the feature flag.

ben: :thumbsup: assign me for review please. We should aim to merge before EOD if CI is green — low risk.

ci-bot: Updated PR CI: 44/44 passed. Canary rollout scheduled for 2026-03-18 14:00 PT (2pm PT).

sara: Thanks — I'll add a docs blurb to /docs/api/params.md and put a short note in release notes about the new flag + behavior.

liam: One more: add tests that exercise temperature/top_p interactions. For very low temp + high top_p we should still respect stop precedence and ensure logprobs computed for the terminating token. Add a matrix test combining stop, max_tokens, temp, top_p.

ben: Will add matrix in tests/generation/param_matrix.yml and include the specific stop-mid-token case.

sara: OK — tagging milestone v1.12.2. I'll ping support and sales to watch logs for any customer reports during the canary rollout.

anna: Thanks all — keep me posted if you need product communication copy for customers on Dedicated.

liam: I'll monitor canary and post perf numbers. If all good we flip default for hosted in the next release.

ben: Simple follow-up: add a short unit test for streaming code path that simulates partial token flush. That caught it in local once.

sara: Added that in the PR. Merging after final review. :rocket:
